To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vitamin D3 supplementation (2000 IU/day) in combination with weight loss of at least 10% was associated with significant decreases in levels of the proinflammatory cytokine, IL6.

(i) vitamin D3 supplementation (2000 IU/day) did not significantly affect inflammatory biomarkers in postmenopausal overweight and obese women, and (ii) weight loss, particularly ≥10% weight loss, was associated with significantly greater decreases in serum levels of inflammatory biomarkers, including IL6 and IL1β.

vitamin D3 supplementation, in combination with weight loss of at least 10% of body weight in overweight and obese postmenopausal Caucasian women with 25(OH) D concentrations of 10 to 32 ng/mL, was associated with a reduction in levels of IL-6, a proinflammatory cytokine that is elevated in obesity, and may be associated with risk of several cancers.

the effects of weight loss, vitamin D3, and weight loss combined with vitamin D3 supplementation, on inflammatory biomarkers in postmenopausal overweight women.
the effects of vitamin D on the immune system.

vitamin D is associated with a lower risk of cancer, and that this is likely due to a reduction of cancer incidence and not mortality.
the results of the current study are not sufficient to recommend vitamin D supplementation to postmenopausal overweight women.
vitamin D supplementation is beneficial in the prevention and treatment of cancer and other diseases, and is safe and inexpensive, and that the current RDA is far too low.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vitamin D supplementation in combination with a modest weight loss of 5% or more is associated with a decrease in inflammatory biomarkers.
vitamin D supplementation in combination with a weight loss program was associated with a decrease in IL6, which was most pronounced in those that lost at least 5%.

vitamin D supplementation in combination with modest weight-loss was associated with significant decreases in levels of the inflammatory biomarker IL6, and that these changes in IL6 levels were not associated with significant changes in the other inflammatory biomarkers, TNFα or IL8, or with changes in the composite score.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vitamin D3 in combination with weight loss may have an anti-inflammatory effect, which may have important health benefits.
the combination of vitamin D3 and weight loss is a safe, effective way to reduce levels of IL6, a marker of inflammation, in postmenopausal overweight/obese women with low 25(OH) D levels.
vitamin D supplementation in combination with modest weight loss is associated with reductions in levels of inflammatory biomarkers.
